title: Electronic Ballast and Diffuser Change for the Fluorescent Ceiling and Wall Wash Lighting

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: High-frequency electronic ballast and a prismatic diffuser for the fluorescent ceiling and wall wash lighting, released to stop the visible flicker and the short tube life reported on high-utilisation aircraft.

sections.reason: Cabin crew and passengers reported visible flicker in the ceiling and wall wash lighting, particularly at the dimmed setting used during boarding, and tube life was running at about 4000 flight hours against a nominal 9000. The magnetic ballast fitted at build runs the tube at line frequency, which is close enough to the flicker fusion threshold to be seen at low output, and its starting characteristic blackens the tube ends. Fifty-two cabin defect reports were logged against the lighting in a single year across one operator of 34 aircraft.
sections.description: The magnetic ballast is replaced by a high-frequency electronic unit housed in the existing stowage envelope D3320117509271, and the tube is fitted behind a prismatic diffuser that widens the wall wash pattern and hides the tube outline. The shear head bolts LN983579-8C at the ballast mounting are replaced by a shorter grip because the electronic unit is thinner, and the curtain rail sub-assembly D3320000585452 is re-drilled where the new diffuser clip lands. The wall wash lining FIN 9RH is unchanged and the lighting panel FIN 51RH keeps its dimming input. Work is done from inside the cabin in zones 265, 271 and 291 with the ceiling panels lowered.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 3.1 kg per aircraft. Electrical load falls by 210 VA because the electronic ballast is appreciably more efficient. The ballast is interchangeable at unit level and the two types may be mixed along the cabin, although the colour temperature differs slightly and operators were advised to convert a full zone at a time. Measured flicker at the dimmed setting falls below the perception threshold and tube life reached 8600 flight hours in the trial fleet. IPC content for ATA 33-20 was re-issued.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through a single bulletin, at about sixteen hours per aircraft with the ceiling panels lowered. The modification has since been superseded by the solid state lighting standard and is no longer offered for new embodiment, although ballast spares remain available.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, no measurable CG effect
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the line had already moved to a different lighting standard
